title: The derby, off season
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The CRAB DERBY sign at the shack, painted over for winter with one word: CLOSED. Gully painted it. The crab shows through. Wood says leave it.

panels.composition: The shack. The hand-painted CRAB DERBY sign, and over it in fresh white paint: CLOSED. The crab showing through the white. GULLY with the brush.

image.prompt: a hand-painted crab derby sign on a shingle shack painted over in fresh white with a single word, the crab shape showing through, a teenager holding a paintbrush, black and white, no words
image.notes: Letter after: CLOSED, one word, over the sign.

panels.composition: The crab through the paint. A ghost of hatching.

image.prompt: close on a painted-over sign with the shape of a crab showing faintly through white paint, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Gully, brush up for another coat. Wood's hand stopping him.

image.prompt: a young man's hand stopping a teenager's paintbrush before a whitewashed sign, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The sign from the road: CLOSED, and a crab under it, faint. The shack. October. The strip's first ghost.

image.prompt: a small bait shack seen from the road with a whitewashed sign reading one word and a faint crab beneath the paint, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: CLOSED over the crab. The crab shows through. 'That's why.'
